4851.title: Sculpture of 'Laocoon and his sons', also known as the 'Laocoon group'. Excavated in Rome in 1506 it is a prime example of classical sculpture. The style of the sculpture is Hellenistic "Pergamene baroque". The original is Marble, but it is unclear whether this is a stereoscopic photo of the original or of a copy, which may have been made from an alternative material. The statue has since been altered by removal of restored parts, thought not to conform to original intentions, which were removed in the 1980s. The scene depicted is debated as to whether it is from the Greek Epic Cycle, or Virgil's Aeneid. It was displayed at the Great Exhibition in 1851.

154998.title: Crucifixion
154998.creator: attributed to workshop of Nicolas II Palardin, attributed to workshop of Martin Fiacre

editorial.note: This Crucifixion is carved from a deep black marble found only in Wallonia (Belgium). The Palardin-Fiacre family of sculptors (originally from Lombardy), who were active in Liège, specialized in reliefs made from this hard-towork material.

The god Bacchus, accompanied by a satyr with a torch, discovers the sleeping Ariadne and falls in love with the princess. It is hardly a coincidence that Cupid, the god of love, is seated in the foreground.
The Brussels sculptor Gerard van Opstal created a stir at the French court in Paris with his small-scale ivory reliefs in the Flemish Baroque style of Rubens.
These figures were part of a large altar in the chapel of the Confraternity of Our Lady in ‘s Hertogenbosch. This was a highly innovative altar, with its lively, expressive scenes and figures.
